purpose: Freeze a finite issuer-as-passenger-transportation-provider booking, reservation, ticketing, check-in, boarding, trip completion, disruption, reaccommodation, baggage, refund and compensation lifecycle before source rows, passenger or journey values, formulas, directions, comparators, security prices or returns.

repository_evidence.bounded_search_scope: Campaign160 inventory and Campaign163-202 source-frontier metadata only
repository_evidence.fleet_right_milestone_and_incident_bound: Campaign166, Campaign167, Campaign179 and Campaign186 freeze issuer incidents, discrete operating milestones, route or slot rights and shipping fleet or charter states. A route opening, license, slot, vehicle or vessel, broad outage or maintenance event does not preserve passenger reservation, ticket, check-in, boarding, journey, baggage, reaccommodation and compensation identities across the complete traveler population.
repository_evidence.operating_kpi_boundary: Campaign168 freezes passenger counts, service volume, utilization and load factor as generic recurring operating KPIs. Aggregate boardings, passenger-kilometers, departures, arrivals or on-time percentages do not preserve bookings, waitlists, changes, cancellations, no-shows, denied boardings, missed connections and completed-trip denominators.
repository_evidence.customer_quality_and_support_boundary: Campaign170 freezes satisfaction, complaints, refunds and retention outcomes, while Campaign199 freezes support-ticket stock flow and SLA clocks. A survey score, complaint or service ticket cannot substitute for the provider's underlying ticket, journey, baggage, disruption and duty-of-care state.
repository_evidence.pricing_payment_loyalty_and_accounting_b: Campaign169 freezes fares, surcharges, yields and selling terms; Campaign195 freezes authorization, clearing, refund and settlement rails; Campaign197 freezes miles and reward obligations. Fare revenue, receivables, deferred revenue, card payments, refunds or loyalty redemptions do not establish reservation, carriage, reaccommodation, baggage or statutory compensation fulfillment.
repository_evidence.generic_service_lifecycle_boundary: Campaign201 and Campaign202 show that appointment or application stock-flow operators do not create a cross-sector factor. Passenger carriage has distinct itinerary, segment, ticket coupon, equipment, station or port, boarding, transfer, baggage and transport-right semantics and requires its own complete source contract.
repository_evidence.privacy_and_lawful_use_boundary: No directly identifiable passenger name record, travel document, itinerary, precise movement history, payment credential, loyalty identity, disability or assistance record, immigration or security record may be acquired or used. Any admitted source must be lawful, licensed or public, deidentified and aggregated enough to avoid re-identification while preserving the frozen point-in-time issuer-state contract.
repository_evidence.sector_scope_boundary: Applicable listed airline, passenger rail, intercity bus, ferry and other scheduled passenger-transport service providers, listed parents and material operating subsidiaries must be frozen point in time. Cargo-only logistics, shipping-fleet, airport or station landlord, vehicle manufacturer and structurally inapplicable issuers may not be filled with zero or cross-sector ranked.
repository_evidence.point_in_time_boundary: A current timetable, route map, booking dashboard, passenger manifest, ticket record, baggage status or compensation balance cannot be projected backward without reservation, ticketing, schedule, check-in, boarding, departure, transfer, arrival, disruption, baggage, refund, compensation, correction and first-public or first-licensed-availability histories.
